headline: South Asia: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting.
- India: IndiGo Extends Saudi Flight Cancellations Till October 27 Amid Houthi Attacks.
- Persian Gulf Region: European, Middle East ministers urge US-Iran diplomacy, not new attacks.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US military needs ‘urgent revolutionary institutional change’ to prepare for modern war, Petraeus says.
- Military Times, one hour ago: US military needs ‘urgent revolutionary institutional change’ to prepare for modern war, Petraeus says.
Ret. Army Gen. David Petraeus praised the Pentagon’s new Autonomous Warfare Command but said the U.S. must rapidly prepare for modern autonomous war.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ‘You can’t just live for yourself’ - 88-y-o Merle Stern awarded for decades of community service.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: ‘You can’t just live for yourself’ - 88-y-o Merle Stern awarded for decades of community service.
At 88, Merle Stern has little interest in measuring her life by the accolades she has racked up. For the retired justice of the peace, the greater reward has been the opportunity to help people through their difficulties, restore relationships, and ensure that the needs of the vulnerable are not overlooked.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Messi wins Princess of Asturias award for sporting, humanitarian work.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 4 hours ago: Messi wins Princess of Asturias award for sporting, humanitarian work.
The 2022 World Cup winner, the first Argentine athlete to receive the prize, said his late father was ‘very excited about’ the award La entrada Messi wins Princess of Asturias award for sporting, humanitarian work se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Zelenskyy says restrictions on Starlink remain in force.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Zelenskyy says restrictions on Starlink remain in force.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy has confirmed that technical caps on Starlink remain active, while delayed missile interceptor deliveries complicate Ukraine’s defence against daily Russian strikes.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Three injured and infrastructure damaged in Russians attack on Odesa Oblast – photos.
Oleh Kiper has reported that Russian strikes hit civilian, recreational and industrial facilities in southern Odesa Oblast, injuring three people.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Ukrainian sailor killed and three missing as vessel sinks off Romanian coast after drone attack.
The Ukrainian Embassy in Romania is coordinating with local authorities following the sinking of the Comoros-flagged ship, which left several crew members missing or hospitalised.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russia launches series of strikes on Kharkiv, injuring two kids and damaging buildings – photos, video.
Russian forces launched repeated drone strikes on Kharkiv, damaging residential buildings, a circus structure and cars and injuring a girl and a boy.
Southern Europe - bottom line: ARTE Europe Weekly: Should the EU Sanction Israel Over Violence in the West Bank?.
- Balkan Insight, 8 hours ago: ARTE Europe Weekly: Should the EU Sanction Israel Over Violence in the West Bank?.
Occupation, displacement and war crimes: according to the UN, radical Israelis in the West Bank are violating international law.
- Politico Europe, 18 hours ago: Can Europe save the world’s war crimes court from Trump?.
U.S. President Donald Trump has the world’s war crimes court in his crosshairs. By sanctioning the entire International Criminal Court, his administration is threatening its ability to function. Europe has rushed to the court’s defense — but can it actually protect it from American financial power? And how far is the European Union willing to […]
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Ukraine and Russia each exchange 270 prisoners of war.
Kyiv thanked the United States and the United Arab Emirates for facilitating the third stage of the swap.
- Politico Europe, 8 hours ago: French prosecutors open hate crime probe after deadly drive-by shooting.
The incident, which killed at least one person, is being treated as a possible act of terror.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: European, Middle East ministers urge US-Iran diplomacy, not new attacks.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: European, Middle East ministers urge US-Iran diplomacy, not new attacks.
An escalation would 'create nothing but losers', French foreign minister says as US official warns of possible strike.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Turkey says renewed attack on Iran would expand conflict, diplomacy only way.
Leaders from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Germany, France, Britain, and Italy met in Istanbul on Friday to discuss developments in the Iran war.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Netanyahu warns Israel could face banking sanctions, prepares alternative financial system.
Netanyahu says Israel is preparing alternatives to banking sanctions, including blockchain, and warns that US military aid cannot be taken for granted.
- Jerusalem Post, 7 hours ago: Netanyahu vows to hunt Hamas terrorists as ministers demand major West Bank military operation.
Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich claimed that, after the attack, there would be "no escaping" a comprehensive military campaign in the West Bank.
Africa - bottom line: Gaza: Moment Israeli airstrike hits building in Nuseirat caught on camera.
- Africanews, 10 hours ago: Gaza: Moment Israeli airstrike hits building in Nuseirat caught on camera.
Footage captures the moment an Israeli strike hits a building in Gaza's Nuseirat camp. No deaths were reported, but images show a wounded person.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 15 hours ago: Mali: Army, Russia's 'Africa Corps' Commit New Abuses.
[HRW] Nairobi -- Unlawful Drone Strike, Torture of Civilians in Mopti Region
- Africanews, 7 hours ago: Tigray is still at war, rebel leader warns, claiming tactical victories.
The leader of Ethiopia’s rebel Tigray People’s Liberation Front says the northern state is still at war. In a message aired on Tigrayan television on Wednesday, Debretsion Gebremichael said the TPLF is continuing to fight federal forces in the region and will “remain a graveyard for its enemies.”
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 9 hours ago: Liberia: New Equipment, New Opportunities - Liberia-Morocco Military Partnership Takes a Step Forward!.
[New Republic] A Moroccan C-130 cargo aircraft touched down at Roberts International Airport on October 19, bringing military vehicles and logistical supplies for the Armed Forces of Liberia, according to published reports.

[SAnews.gov.za] Nelson Mandela Bay Mayor Babalwa Lobishe has welcomed the acceptance of the final scoping report for Eskom's proposed 5 200-megawatt nuclear power plant at Thyspunt in the Kouga Local Municipality, Eastern Cape.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: Malawi: Schools Urged to Adapt As Heatwave Warning Issued Across Malawi.
[Nyasa Times] Schools and other learning institutions have been urged to implement immediate measures to protect learners and staff following a heatwave alert issued by the Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services (DCCMS).
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 10 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Teen Who Axed Aunt to Death Over Witchcraft Suspicions Acquitted of Murder.
[New Zimbabwe] An 18-year-old man who killed his 60-year-old aunt with an axe over witchcraft allegations has been acquitted of murder by the High Court after psychiatric examinations found him mentally disturbed at the time of the killing.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting.
Developments in the Gulf region amid the US-Israeli war on Iran came under discussion as the R4 foreign ministers — Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye — met with their counterparts from France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom. The R4 group, comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia have completed ratification of Makkah defence pact: FO.
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have completed the ratification processes for the Makkah defence pact while Turkiye was in the process of doing so, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Friday. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: 10 India-sponsored terrorists killed as bid to undermine state's writ in Gwadar foiled: ISPR.
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday that 10 India-sponsored terrorists were killed in separate engagements as security forces thwarted their attempts to “undermine the writ of the state” in Balochistan’s Gwadar district.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, Times of India - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, Jerusalem Post, ABC News Australia, 4 hours ago: West Bank attack wounds 5 Israelis as Netanyahu cancels events.
An attack in the occupied West Bank wounded at least five Israelis on Friday and triggered a shootout that left two Palestinians dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel political events days ahead of elections. An AFP journalist who witnessed the firefight saw two Palestinian men in casual attire and armed with a handgun and an automatic rifle exchanging fire with Israeli forces at a checkpoint near the Palestinian city of Hebron. The journalist reported that Israeli forces eventually shot and killed the attackers.
India - bottom line: IndiGo Extends Saudi Flight Cancellations Till October 27 Amid Houthi Attacks.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: IndiGo Extends Saudi Flight Cancellations Till October 27 Amid Houthi Attacks.
The flight disruptions come amid escalating drone and missile strikes targeting Saudi Arabia's airports, energy installations and other critical infrastructure, with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis having been involved in a prolonged campaign against the country.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: 'Jihadist, Fake': Trump Attacks Michigan Senate Candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
Speaking to reporters on the White House South Lawn before leaving for a campaign rally in Florida, Trump said he was looking forward to visiting Michigan and campaigning for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: US Could "Absolutely" Strike Iran This Weekend, Says Envoy.
Trump has also signalled an openness to resuming strikes on Iran after a long deadlock in diplomacy.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: US Preparing To Resume Large-Scale Strikes Against Iran: Report.
Washington and Tehran's forces have settled into a pattern of strikes on commercial ships, with the United States seeking to enforce a blockade of Iran's ports and the Islamic Republic trying to exert control over the key Strait of Hormuz waterway.
Asia - bottom line: Macron condemns ‘racist terrorist attack’ after deadly shooting near Paris.
- South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, ABC News Australia, Africanews, Jerusalem Post, The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: Macron condemns ‘racist terrorist attack’ after deadly shooting near Paris.
A gunman firing from his car killed one person and wounded five – including a 12-year-old girl shot eight times – in the Paris suburbs on Friday, in what the French presidency condemned as a “racist terrorist attack”. French President Emmanuel Macron visited the working-class town of Trappes southwest of Paris, where a gunman opened fire earlier in the day in an attack suspected of having targeted people of foreign origin. This was a “racist, terrorist attack”, the Elysee presidential palace...
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Gunmen kill 7 at Jordan church, king vows retaliation.
Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded dozens at a church in southern Jordan on Friday, authorities said, with the king vowing retaliation for the rare attack on Christians in the majority Sunni Muslim kingdom. Assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate and opened fire, authorities said. The gunmen got out of a vehicle and started shooting during a funeral procession, the public security directorate said in a statement,...
- Taipei Times, just now: China using militia boats to ramp up war readiness.
- South China Morning Post - China, Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Melania Trump brokers ceasefire in Russian-occupied Ukraine city, White House says.
US first lady Melania Trump has brokered a coming ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the war-ravaged Ukrainian city of Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid and the evacuation of civilians, the White House announced on Friday. The localised ceasefire is set to begin Thursday, with the American first lady saying in a news release that the situation there is “on the brink of disaster”. AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Threats against politicians are on the rise. How can we move to a better, safer politics?.
- The Guardian - Australia, 6 hours ago: Threats against politicians are on the rise. How can we move to a better, safer politics?.
The alleged attack on independent MP Helen Haines has horrified Australia. But around the world, politicians and women in particular face increased threats to their safety “Thoughts and prayers.” After each soul-destroying mass shooting in the United States, this is the platitude invariably trotted out by every impotent politician unable to confront the stranglehold reality of the country’s gun lobby. “Turn the temperature down,” risks becoming Australia’s equivalent.
- ABC News Australia, 13 hours ago: Rebel Wilson wins second court case with company awarded $10.
UK production firm, AI Film, has lost its legal bid to sue actor Rebel Wilson in the Supreme Court for $15 million.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: ABC 50/50 quiz: Testing your knowledge of Sense and Sensibility, Martian moons and whale parts.
Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, the other is wrong. But be warned: we might try to trick you.
- The Guardian - Australia, 2 hours ago: Back to Back Barries: Do our leaders have the courage to take on their base? – video.
Tony Barry and George Megalogenis (filling in for Barrie Cassidy) examine the response to the horrific alleged attack on independent MP Helen Haines this week. While the prime minister pleaded for all to 'turn the temperature' down, it didn't take long for some to dial it right up. So can politicians from all sides tell their tribes to tone down the hateful rhetoric? And what lessons can we learn from history to help us all navigate toxic public debate? Continue reading...

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
